## formal
\emph{Setting and conditions.} Assume the representatives of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}, so that the towers that admit matter have space dimension $D_{r} = 3$ for this world ($r = 6$) and the mirror ($r = 2$), $D_{r} = 2$ for $r = 1, 7$ and $D_{r} = 4$ for $r = 3, 5$; assume, as the stored total does, that all six are populated (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}) and that residues $0$ and $4$ are empty (the single-ideal clause, Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(vi)); and assume the stored sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}, which rests on Premise P1, \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}). A \emph{filling} gives each populated tower a quantum mass $m_{r} > 0$ and a number $\nu_{r} > 0$ of quanta per unit volume of its own space. Fix one length $d$, common to all towers and independent of the filling. With the sourcing rule read through a length $\lambda d$ of the extra direction of a five-dimensional tower and with a three-dimensional tower's sheets $\mu d$ apart, the shares and the total are
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{m_{r}\nu_{r}}{m_{6}\nu_{6}} \times
\begin{cases} \lambda d & D_{r} = 4, \\ 1 & D_{r} = 3, \\ 1/(\mu d) & D_{r} = 2, \end{cases}
\qquad
T \;=\; \sum_{r \neq 6} f_{r} .
\]
Premise R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) is $m_{r} = m$ for all $r$; R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) is $\nu_{r} V_{D_{r}} d^{D_{r}} = 1$, with $V_{D}$ the volume of the unit ball $\B^{D}$. \emph{Reading of R3.} R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) says ``one cell radius''. It is read here as $\lambda = \mu = 1$ in the fixed length $d$, not in each tower's own cell radius $a_{r}$, defined by $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}a_{r}^{D_{r}} = 1$. Under R2 the two readings coincide ($a_{r} = d$); they differ as soon as R2 is varied, and the stored wording does not choose between them. Write $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$, \emph{equal mass per ball of radius $d$}, for the statement that $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}}$ takes one value on all populated towers.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(One density law; proved, under the fixed-length reading of R3.)} R1 and R2 together imply $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. Under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ and R3 so read, $f_{r} = V_{3}/V_{D_{r}}$ and $T = (11\pi + 16)/3\pi$, the total of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}; with the thicknesses free, $T = 1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$, as in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}. $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ implies neither R1 nor R2: for positive numbers $s_{r}$ that are constant on the reversal orbits, with $s_{2} = s_{6} = 1$ and $s_{1} = s_{7}$, $s_{3} = s_{5}$ not both $1$, the filling $m_{r} = s_{r}m$, $\nu_{r} = 1/(s_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$ satisfies $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$, violates R1 and R2, and has every share and the total unchanged. It leaves the mirror pair as the population count has it and keeps every equality along the reversal orbits, so it is a model of P1, P2, P3, P4, the common ceiling coupling and R3 in the fixed-length reading (argued for P2: the model equates along the orbits whatever counts as a sector label). So, under that reading, every share depends on R1 and R2 only through $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. \emph{Under the other reading this fails.} If the thickness is one own cell radius $a_{r}$, then
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{m_{r}}{m_{6}}\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{D_{r}}}\,\Bigl(\frac{a_{6}}{a_{r}}\Bigr)^{3},
\]
which $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ does not fix: with $s_{3} = s_{5} = 16$ and $s_{r} = 1$ elsewhere, $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ holds and the total is $11/3 + 32/3\pi \approx 7.06$. On that reading R2 is used twice, once in the density and once to supply R3's unit, and the shares depend on $m_{r}/a_{r}^{3}$. The stored results that use R1 or R2 separately (the common mass and the cell radius in the cluster bound, R2's number density in the odd towers' population and survival) are not statements of the total.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Democracy of the total mass; proved, given the reading of the stored sphere form.)} Read a tower's mass per unit measure of its Euclidean de Sitter sphere $\Sph^{D_{r}+1}$ as its mass per unit volume of its space divided by one length common to all towers, as the stored sphere form does. Then the total mass of tower $r$ on the sphere of radius $\ell$ is a common factor times $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}\ell^{D_{r}}$, by $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$. Hence the democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}) is $(\mathrm{E}_{\ell})$, the same kind of law at the de Sitter radius, and with the thickness $\ell$ it gives the same shares (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}). The law and the thickness are tied through one length: $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ with thickness $d'$ gives $V_{3}/V_{D_{r}} \times (d'/d)^{D_{r}-3}$. $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ and $(\mathrm{E}_{\ell})$ are different statements for $d \neq \ell$ and neither implies the other: under R1 and R2 in the length $d$ the total masses on the spheres are in the ratio $(\ell/d)^{D_{r}}$, unequal across dimensions, and the democracy premise leaves $m_{r}$ and $\nu_{r}$ separately free.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The mirror's term is obtained twice; the premise sets are audited.)} At $D_{r} = 3$, $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ gives $f_{2} = 1$ through the sourcing rule. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i) gives $f_{2} = 1$ from Premises P1, P2, the common ceiling coupling and the copy of content, with P4 discharged for the mirror, and without R1, R2 or R3. The two derivations share P1 (through the sourcing rule), P2 and P3 among the subject's postulates; the first does not have P4 or the common ceiling coupling under it, the second not R1, R2 or R3. So restricted to the reversal pair $\{2, 6\}$, $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ is a consequence of the population count, and it is a premise only on the four odd towers. The two agree exactly on the proton-only branch; on the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) the population count gives $f_{2} = 931.8/936.7 \approx 0.9948$ (the stored $0.995$), so R1 read as equal mean mass per baryon fails there by about one part in two hundred and the total is smaller by about $1/200$; both values lie within one standard deviation ($0.065$) of the record's $5.364$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What still moves the total; proved.)} With $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ kept: thicknesses $(\lambda, \mu) = (2, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$ give $11/3 + 32/3\pi$ and $7/3 + 16/3\pi$, each more than five standard deviations from the record; one quantum per cube of side $2d$ in place of the ball, with thickness one side, gives exactly $5$, more than five standard deviations below; a three-dimensional tower read at $D_{r} = 4$ gives $7/3 + 8/\pi$. So R3, the shape of the cell and the dimensions of P3 are each used.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Count; audited on the stored dependence edges and a text search.)} Among the twenty-three postulates of the dark-matter subject: the past cone of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} contains five on its stored edges, P2, P3, R1, R2, R3, and six with P1, which enters through the sourcing rule that the proposition's proof uses and its edges do not record. The past cone of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}, which takes the mirror's term from the population count, contains seven, P1, P2, P3, P4, R1, R2 and the common ceiling coupling, and eight with R3 as the choice $\lambda = \mu = 1$; the restatements \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-unit-ball-rule} and \claimref{simulations.imported-unit-ball-rule-family} have the same five and eight. A third stored statement of the same total, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}, has the democracy premise and R3. The union over these stored statements of the total is nine; fourteen of the twenty-three lie under none of them. Of the fourteen, four lie under stored results that vary the conditions of the total: P5 (\claimref{synthesis.no-rule-p2-licenses-gives-the-thickness-of-r3}), H1 (\claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}), and H1, H2 and Premise U (\claimref{synthesis.bott-shifted-model-leaves-the-odd-towers-dimension-free}); the remaining ten (CPT covariance, the flag as datum, Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower, the six modelling premises of the cluster simulations and the registered asymmetry) lie under no stored result whose text contains the value $5.364$ or its closed form. The statements of the total were found by that text pattern, which misses statements by reference (the third above was added by hand), so ``under none'' is audited on the search, not proved. The cones also contain postulates of other subjects: under the closed form the four foundation premises (\claimref{synthesis.premise-the-bit}, \claimref{synthesis.premise-minimal-non-commutativity}, \claimref{synthesis.premise-superposition-over-the-integers}, \claimref{synthesis.continuum-completion-premise}); the population-count route adds \claimref{dark-matter.hyp-u-equal-rank-one-eigenvalues} (subject neutrinos), \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series}, \claimref{sheaf.tameness}, \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} and \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}. Three conditions of the closed form are held as text and not as edges: the sourcing rule with P1, the single-ideal clause and the population of the odd towers. By (i) to (iii), under the fixed-length reading, the subject's premises of the total reduce to: P1 for the sourcing rule; P3 for the dimensions; $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ on the four odd towers; R3; and for the mirror's term either $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ on the reversal pair or P2 and the common ceiling coupling. The total remains a fit: $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ and R3 fix the two odd shares $4/3$ and $8/3\pi$ against one measured number.
\end{enumerate}

## technical
The stored total of dark to baryonic matter is a sum of shares, each the ratio of a tower's mass density, read per unit of this world's volume by the sourcing rule (which rests on P1), to ours. Assume the counted thickness of R3 is one fixed length common to all towers, the length in which the cell of R2 is measured, and not each tower's own cell radius; under R2 the two are the same, and the store's wording, one cell radius, does not say which is meant when R2 is varied. Under that reading a share sees R1 (equal quantum masses) and R2 (one quantum per unit ball) only through their product, equal mass per ball of that radius: a filling in which the odd towers' quanta are heavier by a factor and rarer by the same factor violates both and has the same shares. Under the other reading the statement fails: the same kind of filling, with the five-dimensional towers' quanta sixteen times heavier and rarer, moves the total to about $7.06$. The democracy premise, equal total mass on each tower's de Sitter sphere, is the same kind of law at the de Sitter radius, by $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$ and given the stored reading of the sphere form; with the thickness equal to that radius it gives the same shares, and neither law implies the other. The mirror's share of one is obtained twice: from the density law at dimension three, and from the population count under P1, P2 and the common ceiling coupling; the two share P1, P2 and P3 among the subject's premises. On the burning branch the second gives about $0.995$, so they disagree there by about half a percent, inside the error bar. The thickness, the ball shape of the cell and the dimensions of P3 each move the total when changed. On the stored dependence edges, five of the subject's twenty-three postulates lie under the closed form (six with P1, held for it as text), eight under the total with the mirror's term taken from the population count, and the democracy premise with R3 under a third stored statement; fourteen lie under no stored statement of the total found by the search, four of them under results that vary its conditions. The cones also hold the four foundation premises and five postulates of other subjects, and the closed form assumes, as text, that the odd towers are populated and that residues $0$ and $4$ are empty. The total remains a fit.

## lay
The series fits the measured ratio of dark matter to ordinary matter, 5.364, with a rule built on several assumptions. This result sorts out which assumptions the number uses. Two of them, that all hidden worlds have quanta of the same mass and that each holds one quantum per unit ball, matter for the number only through their product, the mass per unit ball, as long as the counted thickness is a fixed common length; if the thickness is instead each world's own spacing, this is no longer true and the same change of filling moves the number to about 7. A third assumption, equal total mass in every world, is the same kind of law with a cosmic unit of length, and gives the same shares given the stored reading of it. The share of the mirror world is derived twice, by two routes that agree to within about half a percent. Of the twenty-three assumptions filed under dark matter, at most eight stand under the number on either route, besides the series' foundation premises and five assumptions filed elsewhere, and assuming also that the hidden worlds are populated as the rule supposes. Under all of this the ratio is still fitted, not predicted: two shares are chosen and one number is matched.

## one-liner
Under the stored sourcing rule, and given R3's thickness read as one fixed common length $d$ (not each tower's own cell radius, where the claim fails and the same refilling gives $7.06$), every share of the dark-to-baryon total depends on R1 and R2 only through equal mass per ball of radius $d$; the democracy premise is that law at the de Sitter radius, given the stored sphere reading; the mirror's term follows twice; five (six with P1) of the subject's twenty-three postulates lie under the closed form, eight under the population-count route, and the total remains a fit.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{(i).} The shares of the Setting are the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} (a five-dimensional tower's density times the length of its extra direction; a sheet family's density per unit area over the spacing), divided by this world's density. Throughout (i) the thickness is $\lambda d$, $\mu d$ in the fixed length $d$. Under R1 and R2, $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}} = m$ for every $r$, which is $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. Under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ with common value $\kappa$, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = \kappa/(V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$, so
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{V_{3}\,d^{3}}{V_{D_{r}}\,d^{D_{r}}} \times \bigl(\lambda d,\; 1,\; 1/(\mu d)\bigr)
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{D_{r}}} \times \bigl(\lambda,\; 1,\; 1/\mu\bigr)
\]
for $D_{r} = 4, 3, 2$: the unit $d$ and the value $\kappa$ cancel. With $V_{2} = \pi$, $V_{3} = 4\pi/3$, $V_{4} = \pi^{2}/2$ the shares are $4/3\mu$, $1$, $8\lambda/3\pi$, and the sum over the mirror and the two towers of each odd dimension is $1 + 8/3\mu + 16\lambda/3\pi$, which at $\lambda = \mu = 1$ is $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}; with $\lambda = \mu = c$ it is the function of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}). For the rescaled filling, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = m/(V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}})$ whatever the $s_{r}$, so $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ holds with $\kappa = m$ and each $f_{r}$ is as before, while $m_{r} = s_{r}m$ is not constant and $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}d^{D_{r}} = 1/s_{r} \neq 1$ on an odd pair. Since, with the thickness a fixed length, $f_{r}$ is a function of the products $m_{r}\nu_{r}$ alone, no share separates R1 and R2 from $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$. The model against the other premises: $s_{2} = s_{6} = 1$ leaves the reversal pair's masses, densities and stored charge as they were, so the population count's equalities ($m_{2} = m_{6}$, $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$) hold; $s_{1} = s_{7}$ and $s_{3} = s_{5}$ keep every quantity equal along the reversal orbits, which is all P2 can ask whatever counts as a sector label; P1, P3 and the common ceiling coupling do not mention the odd towers' fillings; P4 is void on the odd residues. \emph{The other reading.} A tower's own cell radius is $a_{r}$ with $\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}a_{r}^{D_{r}} = 1$. With thickness $a_{r}$, a five-dimensional tower's density per unit of our volume is $m_{r}\nu_{r}a_{r} = m_{r}/(V_{4}a_{r}^{3})$ and a three-dimensional tower's is $m_{r}\nu_{r}/a_{r} = m_{r}/(V_{2}a_{r}^{3})$, against ours $m_{6}/(V_{3}a_{6}^{3})$, which is the displayed formula. In the rescaled filling $a_{r} = s_{r}^{1/D_{r}}d$, so $f_{r} = s_{r}^{1 - 3/D_{r}}\,V_{3}/V_{D_{r}}$: with $s_{3} = s_{5} = 16$ the five-dimensional shares double, $a_{r} = 2d$, and $T = 1 + 8/3 + 32/3\pi = 11/3 + 32/3\pi$. (Check 1: two rescalings constant on reversal orbits keep every share in the fixed-length reading; rescaling the mass without the number density moves the total; in the own-radius reading the same fillings give $11/3 + 32/3\pi$ and $17/9 + 32/3\pi$.)

\emph{(ii).} Let $\sigma_{r} = m_{r}\nu_{r}/(2\pi L)$ be the mass per unit $(D_{r}+1)$-measure, with one length $L$ for all towers (the stored sphere form reads one quantum per unit ball as one quantum per unit sphere, the factor $2\pi$ cancelling; any common $L$ serves). The total mass on the sphere of radius $\ell$ is
\[
M_{r} \;=\; \sigma_{r}\,|\Sph^{D_{r}+1}|\,\ell^{D_{r}+1} \;=\; \frac{\ell}{L}\; m_{r}\nu_{r}\,V_{D_{r}}\,\ell^{D_{r}},
\]
using $|\Sph^{D+1}| = 2\pi V_{D}$, which follows from the recursions $V_{D} = (2\pi/D)V_{D-2}$ and $|\Sph^{n}| = (2\pi/(n-1))|\Sph^{n-2}|$ with $V_{0} = 1$, $V_{1} = 2$, $|\Sph^{1}| = 2\pi$, $|\Sph^{2}| = 4\pi$ by induction on $D$. So $M_{r}$ is the same for all populated towers exactly when $m_{r}\nu_{r}V_{D_{r}}\ell^{D_{r}}$ is, which is $(\mathrm{E}_{\ell})$. By (i) the shares under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ with thickness $d$ are the same for every $d$, and with thickness $d'$ each acquires the factor $(d'/d)^{D_{r}-3}$, which is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}'s agreement of the two forms. Under R1 and R2 in the unit $d$, $M_{r} = (\ell/L)\,m\,(\ell/d)^{D_{r}}$, which takes three different values on $D_{r} = 2, 3, 4$ unless $\ell = d$; and the democracy premise constrains only the products $m_{r}\nu_{r}$. (Check 2: the identity for $D = 0$ to $8$ from the two recursions; equal masses at $\ell = d$, the ratios $(\ell/d)^{D+1}$ of the check's normalisation $L = d$ otherwise.)

\emph{(iii).} At $D_{r} = 3$ the share under $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ is $V_{3}/V_{3} = 1$. Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i) states $f_{2} = \epsilon_{2}n_{2}m_{2}/\epsilon_{6}n_{6}m_{6} = 1$ in its own notation, a ratio of mass densities in two three-dimensional spaces, which is $(\mathrm{E}_{d})$ on the pair $\{2, 6\}$ whatever $d$. Its premises are those it names. The first derivation reads the share through the sourcing rule, which rests on P1, so the two share P1, P2 and P3 among the subject's postulates; that the stored cone of the closed form contains neither P4 nor the common ceiling coupling, and that of the population count none of R1, R2 and R3, was read from the stored dependence edges (clause (v)). On the burning branch Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) gives mean masses per baryon $936.7$ and $931.8$ MeV at equal number densities, a ratio $9318/9367 \approx 0.9948$ which it rounds to $0.995$, so $m_{2} \neq m_{6}$ there and the total with that term is smaller by $49/9367$, between $1/200$ and $1/190$. With $3.14159265358 < \pi < 3.14159265359$ both totals lie in $(5.359, 5.365)$, inside $5.364 \pm 0.065$. (Check 3.)

\emph{(iv).} Substitute in the formula of (i): $(\lambda, \mu) = (2, 1)$ gives $1 + 8/3 + 32/3\pi \approx 7.06$ and $(1, 2)$ gives $1 + 4/3 + 16/3\pi \approx 4.03$. For cubic cells of side $2d$, $m_{r}\nu_{r} = m/(2d)^{D_{r}}$, and with thickness $2d$ each odd share is $(2d)^{3}/(2d)^{D_{r}} \times (2d)^{D_{r}-3} = 1$, so $T = 5$, the value the stored note \claimref{note.dark-matter.setting-what-rule-costs} records for cubic cells. A tower with $D_{r} = 2$ read at $D_{r} = 4$ exchanges a term $4/3$ for $8/3\pi$. (Check 4.)

\emph{(v).} The cones were computed from the built graph of the store at the pinned versions, following uses, assumes, founded\_on, specialises and derived\_from edges, and intersected with the list of entities of status postulate and subject dark-matter; the postulates of other subjects in the same cones are listed in the statement. The stored statements of the total and the results that vary it were found by a pattern search of every claim's text for the value $5.364$, $5.3643$ and the closed form (thirteen entities, two of them conjectured observations and one a postulate, with empty cones); Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball}, which states the total by reference, was added by hand, and its cone holds the democracy premise and R3. The cone of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} is P1 alone; Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule} has no edge to it, though its proof and R3 are phrased in the sourcing rule, which is why P1 is counted as text for the closed form. The union over the three routes is P1, P2, P3, P4, R1, R2, R3, the common ceiling coupling and the democracy premise. The fourteen outside it are P5, CPT covariance, the flag as datum, H1, H2, Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower, Premise U, the six modelling premises of the cluster simulations and the registered asymmetry. The reduction is (i) to (iii).

"""synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball: exact checks.

Numbers of Q(pi) are rational functions GA.RF in one variable standing for pi (pi is transcendental, so two such
functions are equal as reals exactly when they are equal as rational functions). Decimal comparisons use the
rational bounds PI_LO < pi < PI_HI. Ball volumes V_D come from V_0 = 1, V_1 = 2, V_D = (2 pi / D) V_(D-2); sphere
measures |S^n| from |S^0| = 2, |S^1| = 2 pi, |S^n| = (2 pi / (n-1)) |S^(n-2)|: two separate recursions.

A filling is, per populated tower, a quantum mass and a number of quanta per unit volume of the tower's own space
(space dimension D = 2, 3 or 4), in one unit of length d. The stored sourcing reads a tower's mass density per unit
of this world's three-volume through a length lam * d of each extra direction (D = 4) or with sheets mu * d apart
(D = 2); the stored premise R3 is lam = mu = 1.

(1) Shares and total from an arbitrary filling; R1 and R2 give V_3/V_D and (11 pi + 16)/(3 pi). Rescaling the mass
    of the odd towers (constant on reversal orbits, the pair {2, 6} untouched) and the number density by the
    inverse factor breaks R1 and R2 and keeps every share WHEN THE THICKNESS IS THE FIXED LENGTH d; rescaling the
    mass alone moves the total; with the thickness one OWN cell radius the same fillings move the total
    (to 17/9 + 32/(3 pi) and to 11/3 + 32/(3 pi)), so the fixed-length reading is a condition, and is tested.
(2) The sphere law (equal mass per unit sphere of the tower's Euclidean spacetime, dimension D + 1) gives the same
    shares, by |S^(D+1)| = 2 pi V_D from the two recursions (D = 0 to 8). The total mass of a tower on its sphere of
    radius ell, filled at one quantum per ball of radius d, is proportional to (ell/d)^(D+1): equal across the three
    dimensions only at ell = d.
(3) The mirror term: 1 from the density law at D = 3; 9318/9367 on the burning branch of the stored mirror share
    (the stored 0.995); the two totals differ by 49/9367, about 1/200, and both lie within one standard deviation of the record's ratio.
(4) Each remaining premise moves the total: thickness (2, 1) and (1, 2); cubic cells of side two units give exactly
    5, more than five standard deviations below the record; a tower moved from D = 2 to D = 4 changes it.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

PI = GA.RF.var()
C = GA.RF.const
PI_LO, PI_HI = F(314159265358, 10 ** 11), F(314159265359, 10 ** 11)
OBS = F(1200, 10000) / F(2237, 100000)        # Omega_c h^2 / Omega_b h^2 of the stored comparison
SIG = F(65, 1000)
ODD_DIMS = [2, 2, 4, 4]                        # residues 1, 7, 3, 5 under the stored representatives
MIRROR_DIM = 3
OUR_DIM = 3


def ball(D):
    V = {0: C(1), 1: C(2)}
    for n in range(2, D + 1):
        V[n] = C(F(2, n)) * PI * V[n - 2]
    return V[D]


def sphere(n):
    S = {0: C(2), 1: C(2) * PI}
    for k in range(2, n + 1):
        S[k] = C(F(2, k - 1)) * PI * S[k - 2]
    return S[n]


def between(x):
    """rational lower and upper bounds of a rational function of pi that is monotone data: evaluate at both ends"""
    a, b = x.eval(PI_LO), x.eval(PI_HI)
    return min(a, b), max(a, b)


def share(D, mass, number, our_mass, our_number, lam=F(1), mu=F(1)):
    """mass density per unit of our three-volume over ours, for a tower of space dimension D"""
    rho = C(mass) * number
    if D == 4:
        rho = rho * C(lam)
    elif D == 2:
        rho = rho / C(mu)
    return rho / (C(our_mass) * our_number)


def total(filling, lam=F(1), mu=F(1)):
    """filling: dict tower -> (D, mass, number density); tower 'us' is this world"""
    _, m0, n0 = filling["us"]
    t = C(0)
    for name, (D, m, n) in filling.items():
        if name != "us":
            t = t + share(D, m, n, m0, n0, lam, mu)
    return t


def unit_ball_filling(scale=None, mass=F(1)):
    """R1 and R2: mass m, one quantum per unit ball; optional per-tower factor s: mass s m, number 1/(s V_D)"""
    towers = {"us": OUR_DIM, "mirror": MIRROR_DIM, "r1": 2, "r7": 2, "r3": 4, "r5": 4}
    out = {}
    for name, D in towers.items():
        s = F(1) if scale is None else scale[name]
        out[name] = (D, mass * s, C(1) / (C(s) * ball(D)))
    return out


CLOSED = (C(11) * PI + C(16)) / (C(3) * PI)


def check_total_depends_on_mass_times_number_only():
    premise("dark-matter.unit-ball-rule")
    premise("dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones")
    base = unit_ball_filling()
    GA.check("R1 and R2 give the stored closed form", total(base).eqrf(CLOSED))
    _, m0, n0 = base["us"]
    GA.check("share 4/3 at D = 2", share(2, *base["r1"][1:], m0, n0).eqrf(C(F(4, 3))))
    GA.check("share 8/(3 pi) at D = 4", share(4, *base["r3"][1:], m0, n0).eqrf(C(F(8, 3)) / PI))
    # rescalings constant on the reversal orbits {1,7}, {3,5}, with the pair {2,6} untouched
    scales = [
        ({"us": F(1), "mirror": F(1), "r1": F(3), "r7": F(3), "r3": F(1, 5), "r5": F(1, 5)},
         C(9) + C(F(16, 15)) / PI, None),
        ({"us": F(1), "mirror": F(1), "r1": F(9), "r7": F(9), "r3": F(16), "r5": F(16)},
         C(25) + C(F(256, 3)) / PI, C(F(17, 9)) + C(F(32, 3)) / PI),
        ({"us": F(1), "mirror": F(1), "r1": F(1), "r7": F(1), "r3": F(16), "r5": F(16)},
         C(F(11, 3)) + C(F(256, 3)) / PI, C(F(11, 3)) + C(F(32, 3)) / PI),
    ]
    roots = {(2, F(9)): F(3), (4, F(16)): F(2), (2, F(1)): F(1), (3, F(1)): F(1), (4, F(1)): F(1)}
    for sc, mass_only, own_radius in scales:
        f = unit_ball_filling(scale=sc)
        GA.check("the pair {2, 6} is untouched and orbits are kept",
                 sc["us"] == sc["mirror"] == 1 and sc["r1"] == sc["r7"] and sc["r3"] == sc["r5"])
        GA.check("the rescaled filling breaks R1", len({v[1] for v in f.values()}) >= 2)
        GA.check("the rescaled filling breaks R2",
                 sum(1 for k in f if not (f[k][2] * ball(f[k][0])).eqrf(C(1))) >= 2)
        GA.check("mass per unit ball is common", all((C(f[k][1]) * f[k][2] * ball(f[k][0])).eqrf(C(1)) for k in f))
        GA.check("every share is kept (thickness in the fixed length)", total(f).eqrf(CLOSED))
        # mass rescaled without the compensating number density: the total moves, to the value computed by hand
        g = {k: (f[k][0], f[k][1], base[k][2]) for k in f}
        GA.check("mass alone moves the total", total(g).eqrf(mass_only) and not mass_only.eqrf(CLOSED))
        if own_radius is not None:
            # thickness one OWN cell radius a_r, with nu_r V_D a_r^D = 1 (a_r rational for these scales)
            t = C(0)
            for k, (D, m, n) in f.items():
                if k == "us":
                    continue
                a = roots[(D, sc[k])]
                GA.check("own cell radius", (n * ball(D) * C(a ** D)).eqrf(C(1)))
                t = t + share(D, m, n, f["us"][1], f["us"][2], lam=a, mu=a)
            GA.check("own-radius reading: (E) holds and the total moves", t.eqrf(own_radius) and not t.eqrf(CLOSED))
    return True


def check_sphere_law_is_the_ball_law_and_fixes_the_unit():
    premise("dark-matter.democracy-de-sitter-radius-unit-ball")
    for D in range(0, 9):
        GA.check("hat-box at D = %d" % D, sphere(D + 1).eqrf(C(2) * PI * ball(D)))
    for D in (2, 3, 4):
        GA.check("sphere share equals ball share at D = %d" % D,
                 (sphere(4) / sphere(D + 1)).eqrf(ball(3) / ball(D)))
    GA.check("sphere measures 2 pi^2, 8 pi^2/3, pi^3",
             sphere(3).eqrf(C(2) * PI * PI) and sphere(4).eqrf(C(F(8, 3)) * PI * PI)
             and sphere(5).eqrf(PI * PI * PI))

    def sphere_mass(D, ell, d):
        # one quantum of unit mass per ball of radius d, read per unit (D+1)-measure with the factor 1/(2 pi d),
        # integrated over the sphere of radius ell
        dens = C(1) / (ball(D) * C(d ** D)) / (C(2) * PI * C(d))
        return dens * sphere(D + 1) * C(ell ** (D + 1))

    for ell, d in [(F(1), F(1)), (F(7, 3), F(7, 3))]:
        ms = [sphere_mass(D, ell, d) for D in (2, 3, 4)]
        GA.check("equal total masses at ell = d", ms[0].eqrf(ms[1]) and ms[1].eqrf(ms[2]))
    for ell, d in [(F(2), F(1)), (F(1), F(3)), (F(5, 4), F(1))]:
        ms = [sphere_mass(D, ell, d) for D in (2, 3, 4)]
        r = ell / d
        GA.check("total masses in ratio (ell/d)^(D+1)",
                 ms[0].eqrf(C(r ** 3)) and ms[1].eqrf(C(r ** 4)) and ms[2].eqrf(C(r ** 5)))
        GA.check("democracy of the total mass fails at ell != d", not ms[0].eqrf(ms[1]))
        # the shares do not see the unit: the filling at radius d has the same total
    return True


def check_mirror_term_is_obtained_twice():
    premise("dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent")
    premise("dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile")
    premise("dark-matter.unit-ball-rule")
    base = unit_ball_filling()
    _, m0, n0 = base["us"]
    GA.check("the density law gives the mirror share one", share(3, *base["mirror"][1:], m0, n0).eqrf(C(1)))
    burning = F(9318, 9367)                     # stored mean masses per baryon 931.8 and 936.7 MeV
    GA.check("the stored 0.995 is this ratio rounded", F(9945, 10000) < burning < F(9955, 10000))
    f = dict(base)
    f["mirror"] = (3, base["mirror"][1] * burning, base["mirror"][2])
    t_burn = total(f)
    deficit = CLOSED - t_burn
    GA.check("the two totals differ by 49/9367, about 1/200",
             deficit.eqrf(C(F(49, 9367))) and F(1, 200) < F(49, 9367) < F(1, 190))
    for t in (CLOSED, t_burn):
        lo, hi = between(t)
        GA.check("within one standard deviation of the record", OBS - SIG < lo and hi < OBS + SIG)
    lo, hi = between(CLOSED)
    GA.check("closed form in (5.36431, 5.36433)", F(536431, 100000) < lo and hi < F(536433, 100000))
    return True


def check_each_remaining_premise_moves_the_total():
    premise("dark-matter.total-function-thickness")
    base = unit_ball_filling()
    t21 = total(base, lam=F(2), mu=F(1))
    t12 = total(base, lam=F(1), mu=F(2))
    GA.check("thickness (2, 1)", t21.eqrf(C(F(11, 3)) + C(F(32, 3)) / PI))
    GA.check("thickness (1, 2)", t12.eqrf(C(F(7, 3)) + C(F(16, 3)) / PI))
    GA.check("both differ from the closed form", not t21.eqrf(CLOSED) and not t12.eqrf(CLOSED))
    lo, hi = between(t21)
    GA.check("thickness (2, 1) is far above the record", lo > OBS + 5 * SIG)
    lo, hi = between(t12)
    GA.check("thickness (1, 2) is far below the record", hi < OBS - 5 * SIG)
    # cubic cells of side 2 (the cube circumscribing the unit ball), thickness one cell side
    towers = {"us": 3, "mirror": 3, "r1": 2, "r7": 2, "r3": 4, "r5": 4}
    cubes = {k: (D, F(1), C(F(1, 2 ** D))) for k, D in towers.items()}
    t_cube = total(cubes, lam=F(2), mu=F(2))
    GA.check("cubic cells give exactly 5", t_cube.eqrf(C(5)))
    GA.check("5 is more than five standard deviations below", F(5) < OBS - 5 * SIG)
    # one three-dimensional tower read at space dimension 4 instead of 2 (a change of representative)
    moved = dict(base)
    moved["r1"] = (4, base["r3"][1], base["r3"][2])
    t_moved = total(moved)
    GA.check("a changed representative moves the total",
             t_moved.eqrf(C(F(7, 3)) + C(8) / PI) and not t_moved.eqrf(CLOSED))
    return True
